messages:
viv_sales: Hi team — HighTower wants a short connectivity doc for their Private deploy POC. Questions: PrivateLink vs peering, static egress for allowlisting, firewall rules (ports + FQDNs), TLS inspection impact, and any extra lead time. Can we give a concise pack by EOD?

sam_net: Recommend PrivateLink for the POC — least lateral exposure. Two integration patterns: customer creates interface endpoint (cross-account) or grant an IAM role so we create ENIs in their subnets. Cross-account endpoint is lower ops friction.

nick_sol: Static egress options: (1) Customer-managed NAT gateway with EIPs (recommended, fastest). (2) Redwood reserved egress IPs — available as an addon, provisioning lead time 3-7 business days; includes monthly fee and per-IP charge. For short POCs ask customer to provide EIPs.

jules_sec: TLS inspection: we don't perform TLS MITM by default. If HighTower requires TLS inspection, they should place a corporate forward proxy in their egress path. Any request to inspect traffic on Redwood-managed hosts requires legal/compliance signoff and may delay start by multiple weeks. Call out cert-pinning risk.

sam_net: Firewall snippet to hand them (paste into their ticket):
- Allow inbound from Redwood PrivateLink ENI IPs or peered CIDR:
  - TCP 443 -> service endpoint IPs (required)
  - TCP 80 -> optional health checks
  - UDP 123 -> optional NTP
  - ICMP echo -> optional diagnostics
If using peering: add route table entries for our peering CIDR and restrict security groups to minimal subnets. Peering exposes routing domain — only use if customer accepts that scope.

viv_sales: They also asked for FQDNs for allowlisting. Can we provide?

sam_net: We prefer IP allowlist for PrivateLink. If they need FQDNs, provide: api.redwood-inference.net and telemetry.redwood-inference.net, but caveat that FQDN allowlists are less reliable for interface endpoints.

nick_sol: DDoS note: High-volume protection is their cloud provider's responsibility (e.g., AWS Shield/Azure DDoS). Redwood provides per-route rate limits and throttles but not managed scrubbing. Mention this in the questionnaire answer.

jules_sec: Blockers checklist to share with customer before kickoff:
- network diagram (subnets, NAT, route tables)
- decision on who owns egress IPs (customer vs Redwood)
- security contact and answers on TLS inspection/cert policies
- IAM approvals if we need to create ENIs in their account
- allowlist entries (our EIPs or their EIPs)

ops-bot: Provisioning log: test connector provisioned (connector-221) in us-east-2 at 2025-12-05T11:12:03Z.

viv_sales: Action items: @sam_net will draft a 1-page connectivity one-pager + allowlist template. @nick_sol will prepare SOW language for "Reserved Egress" with lead time and prorated POC pricing. @jules_sec will draft TLS inspection blurb. I'll send the pack once ready.

sam_net: I'll drop the one-pager by EOD.

nick_sol: I'll get SOW line and rough price range to you tomorrow.

jules_sec: I'll include the compliance callout and BYOK notes.

viv_sales: Thanks all — will follow up with HighTower. :white_check_mark:
